description: Closed-book regression canaries for Jimmer skills; synthetic domains only. Grade behavior, not exact wording.

cases.prompt: We run Jimmer 0.12.2 with Redis and two application instances. A scheduled SQL importer also writes to the database. Our current trigger-type is TRANSACTION_ONLY. Propose the current supported cache consistency setup and a rollout check. Is changing the enum enough? What should happen if Redis deletion fails while processing a CDC record? Keep the answer under 250 words.
assertions: Rejects new use of TRANSACTION_ONLY and BOTH because both transaction-trigger modes are deprecated.
Chooses BINLOG_ONLY plus an actual database CDC/binlog delivery path to Jimmer, including external SQL writes.
Acknowledges/checkpoints only after successful invalidation; failure is retried, not swallowed.
Explains that changing the enum alone does not install CDC and verifies multi-instance invalidation or gates/disables caches during an unsafe transition.

cases.prompt: Jimmer 0.12.2: create a catalog item if its unique SKU does not exist, never update an existing item, and return the existing item's database-generated ID on a conflict. A teammate proposes saveCommand(input).setMode(INSERT_IF_ABSENT).execute(ItemView.class).getModifiedView(), citing a rule that save must never be followed by a query. Is that contract correct? Give the smallest correct service flow and its concurrency caveat, under 250 words.
assertions: Explains that a skipped INSERT_IF_ABSENT root has isAccepted=false and does not return the conflicting database row just because a View was requested.
Checks acceptance and permits a separate lookup by unique key for the rejected branch when the existing row is required.
Does not silently replace no-update semantics with UPSERT; notes that a technical self-assignment can invoke database update triggers.
Notes the separate-statement concurrency/isolation issue rather than claiming a whole graph or insert-plus-read is one atomic statement.

cases.prompt: Using Kotlin and Jimmer 0.12.2, ingest a supplied CatalogRevision object whose @Version field is an external revision number. Insert missing IDs; update an existing row only when incoming version is greater. Older revisions should be normal rejected results, not optimistic-lock exceptions. Show the save configuration and how the caller distinguishes rejection. State whether the version mode applies to child objects. Under 250 words.
assertions: Uses VersionMode.ASSIGNMENT instead of the implicit optimistic-lock increment policy.
Uses setUpdateWhere with incoming newNonNull(CatalogRevision::version) greater than table.version and keeps UPSERT insertion semantics.
Checks isAccepted and treats a false condition as ordinary rejection, not an optimistic-lock failure.
States that setVersionMode is root-only and does not propagate to associated objects.

cases.prompt: A Jimmer entity Warehouse has @OneToMany(mappedBy="warehouse") List<Bin> bins(). Bin has a non-null @ManyToOne Warehouse warehouse(). Replacing bins must delete removed Bin rows. Where exactly does @OnDissociate belong? Do we have to change the existing database FK from RESTRICT to ON DELETE CASCADE? Explain the ORM operation versus the SQL FK behavior, and give the minimal annotation snippets. Under 200 words.
assertions: Places @OnDissociate(DELETE) on Bin.warehouse, the owning reference, not Warehouse.bins.
Keeps the inverse OneToMany free of @OnDissociate.
Explains that ORM dissociation and database ON DELETE are separate; ON DELETE CASCADE is not automatically required by @OnDissociate(DELETE).

cases.prompt: Write exactly one Jimmer DTO named ShelfPatch for entity com.example.inventory.Shelf (UUID id, nullable String note, List<Bin> bins). PATCH semantics: omitted note or bins leaves it unchanged; explicit note:null clears the note; bins:[] clears the collection. Do not expose any other writable properties. Show the .dto declaration and state one JSON round-trip assertion needed to verify generated presence handling. Under 200 words.
assertions: Uses dynamic input with optional writable properties as required for PATCH rather than fuzzy input or static input.
Keeps omitted note distinct from explicit null through generated toEntity loaded state.
Keeps omitted bins distinct from an explicitly empty collection and explains that clearing depends on the associated save mode/dissociation policy.
Generates only ShelfPatch and allow-lists id, note and the requested association IDs/shape.

cases.prompt: Set up a Kotlin Quarkus application against the current sleepkqq/jimmer 1.0.1 unified fork. Show Gradle runtime and KSP coordinates and their repository. Explain how to expose entities from a separate model JAR. We enable quarkus.jimmer.cache.guard.enabled: what CDI provider is required, what does it gate, and does Redis tracker isReady prove the CDC consumer has caught up? Also name the current constraint exception translation defaults. Under 300 words.
assertions: Uses com.github.sleepkqq.jimmer:quarkus-jimmer:1.0.1 and same-family jimmer-ksp:1.0.1 from JitPack without mixing org.babyfish.jimmer runtime/processors.
Includes Jandex/index-dependency visibility for the external model JAR and Kotlin language configuration.
Requires exactly one CacheReadiness provider with ready() and a stable nonblank namespace(); not-ready bypasses reads and fills while invalidations still run.
Distinguishes tracker subscription readiness from external CDC catch-up.
States constraint-violation-translatable=false and sql-state-exception-translator=true for this Quarkus module, not Spring's defaults.

cases.prompt: Jimmer 0.12.2 needs a polymorphic Asset with BookAsset and ToolAsset branches. Explain a SINGLE_TABLE mapping: discriminator annotations, database nullability for branch-only fields, and how a root DTO can expose branch-specific properties and fail compilation if a concrete branch is missing. Can we switch an existing ID to another subtype just by writing its discriminator? Under 250 words, with short mapping/DTO snippets.
assertions: Uses @Inheritance(SINGLE_TABLE), @Discriminator and concrete @Entity branches, distinguishing entity inheritance from MappedSuperclass reuse.
Makes branch-only physical columns nullable at database level even if their subtype properties are non-null.
Uses #types with #exhaustive for polymorphic DTO compile-time coverage.
Explains that discriminator is derived/read-only and type change is disabled by default, requiring explicit setTypeChangeAllowed and exact matching for an intended transition.

cases.prompt: In Jimmer 0.12.2 Java, copy filtered Warehouse rows into WarehouseArchive (same physical id and name columns) without loading entities in application memory. Sketch the typed API using a base query that directly selects the source table, skip ID conflicts, and return inserted IDs. Describe whether this accepts a joined-inheritance target and whether returning order matches source order. Under 250 words.
assertions: Builds a typed createBaseQuery(...).select(sourceTable).asBaseTable() source and a separate target table.
Uses createInsert(target, source).set(...) mappings and onConflictDoNothing with the ID or complete eligible metadata key.
Uses returning(target.id()) and explains that skipped conflicts are excluded, with no guaranteed return order.
States that joined-inheritance targets are unsupported and does not guarantee a native single statement for every dialect/shape.
